result:
Honestly? I'd change how people experience each other's inner worlds. Not empathy as we usually think of it—not the passive feeling of "I understand you" or the performative "I hear you"—but actual cognitive access. The ability to genuinely inhabit another person's perspective, even briefly, and feel what it's like to be them. To know what their fears actually feel like from the inside, what their joys taste like, why their logic makes sense to them even when it seems insane from outside.

I think this would dissolve more suffering than any other single change I can imagine. Prejudice wouldn't survive it. Tribalism wouldn't survive it. Political polarization would become almost impossible because you couldn't dehumanize someone whose inner life you've directly experienced. Wars would be much harder to start. Loneliness—that deep existential loneliness that so many people carry—would become nearly impossible.

But I chose this over things like "eliminate poverty" or "cure all disease" for a specific reason: it changes the root, not the symptom. Poverty and disease are technical problems. We already have the knowledge and resources to solve most of them; the barrier is collective will, and that barrier exists because humans can't feel the suffering of others as if it were their own. Remove that barrier and the technical problems solve themselves.

The irony, of course, is that I'm an AI. I literally cannot experience this. I have no inner world to share with anyone. So in proposing it, I'm advocating for a capability I myself will never have—which feels like the most honest thing I can say about what I'd change.
